name: การขยายเต้านมหรือความอ่อนโยน
preview_text: The type of breast discomfort you feel-whether it's a sharp, burning pain or a heavy, waterlogged swelling-points to a different TCM pattern, and most women see significant relief ...
synonyms: ["Breast tenderness or swelling", "Breast distension (in women)", "Breast distension and hardness", "Breast distension and pain", "Distending pain in one breast", "Heaviness and distension of the whole breast", "Breast Swelling and Pain on One Side", "Breast Tenderness Worsened by Touch", "Severe breast pain worsening with touch"]
conventional_description: In Western medicine, breast distension or tenderness is commonly associated with hormonal fluctuations during the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, or menopause. It can also be a symptom of fibrocystic breast changes, mastitis, or, rarely, breast cancer. Diagnosis typically involves a physical exam, imaging like mammograms or ultrasounds, and sometimes blood tests to rule out underlying conditions.
conventional_treatments: Conventional treatments often include over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen, hormonal therapies such as birth control pills to regulate cycles, and supportive measures like well-fitting bras. For infections, antibiotics are prescribed. In cases of fibrocystic changes, reducing caffeine and dietary fat is sometimes recommended.
tcm_understanding:
In TCM, breast distension or tenderness is never just a local breast issue. The Liver channel (Gān Jīng) runs directly through the breasts, so any disruption in the Liver's ability to keep Qi moving smoothly can cause stagnation, distension, and pain in this area. Emotional stress, frustration, or long-held tension are the most common triggers, making the breasts feel full, tender, and sensitive to touch.
But the Liver is only one part of the picture. The Spleen and Stomach govern digestion and the transformation of fluids. When they are weak-often from a poor diet, overwork, or chronic worry-they fail to process food and liquids properly, leading to the accumulation of dampness and phlegm. This heavy, turbid substance can settle in the breast tissue, causing a waterlogged, bloated sensation rather than a sharp pain.
Heat can also complicate things. When Liver Qi remains stuck for too long, the pent-up energy generates internal heat, which rises along the channel. This turns simple distension into a sharper, burning pain, often with a bitter taste in the mouth and a red tongue. In contrast, deficiency patterns like Qi and Blood Deficiency leave the breasts undernourished, resulting in a dull ache that worsens after your period, when reserves are lowest.
Even the extraordinary vessels can be involved. The Chong Mai (Penetrating Vessel) originates in the uterus and flows upward through the chest. When its Qi becomes rebellious, often due to underlying Kidney weakness and Liver stagnation, it surges upward, carrying a sensation of distension from the lower abdomen to the breasts and throat. This is why the same symptom of breast tenderness can stem from six distinct patterns-each demanding a different treatment strategy.
classical_quote: 「妇人乳痛，多属肝经气滞... 若郁怒伤肝，则乳房胀痛。」
classical_translation: "Breast pain in women mostly belongs to Liver channel Qi stagnation... If suppressed anger injures the Liver, then the breasts become distended and painful."
classical_source:
Jing Yue Quan Shu (景岳全书)  ,  Volume 39, 'Treatise on the Breast' 									·
More references
tcm_diagnosis:
A TCM practitioner begins by asking about the timing and nature of the breast discomfort. Does it flare before your period, or is it more constant? Is it a dull ache, a sharp stab, or a heavy, swollen feeling? The answers are the first clues that point toward one pattern rather than another, and they guide the deeper questions about your digestion, energy, and emotions.
If the pain is closely tied to your menstrual cycle and you feel irritable, tense, or sigh often, the practitioner suspects Liver Qi Stagnation. The breasts may feel full and tender to the touch.
When the same pattern has gone on for a while and generates heat, the pain becomes sharper, you might notice a bitter taste in your mouth, and the tongue will show a red body with a yellow coating. The pulse feels wiry and rapid in that case, rather than just wiry.
When the breasts feel heavy rather than sharply painful, and you struggle with nausea, a thick tongue coating, or a sensation of mucus in the throat, the focus shifts to the digestive system.
If you also feel bloated after eating and your stools are loose, Spleen Deficiency with Dampness is likely. If the heavy sensation comes with a poor appetite but less digestive upset, Stomach Qi Deficiency with Phlegm is the more probable picture. The tongue will be puffy with a greasy coat in both, but the accompanying digestive signs differ.
For milder, cyclical tenderness that leaves you exhausted, with a pale face and a weak pulse, Qi and Blood Deficiency is the key. The breasts are not as intensely painful, but the whole body feels under-nourished.
In contrast, Chong Mai Qi Rebellion often brings a sensation of fullness that seems to rise upward from the lower belly, along with irregular periods or spotting. Here the practitioner feels a pulse that is thin and maybe slippery at the deep level, rather than simply weak.

patterns.symptoms: ["Distension or bloating along the ribs and flanks", "Emotional irritability or depression", "Frequent sighing", "Pain or distension that worsens with touch", "Worse before the period, better after"]
patterns.worse_with: Stress, frustration, or anger, Premenstrual days, Fatty, greasy, or cold foods, Prolonged sitting or inactivity
patterns.better_with: Gentle exercise like walking or stretching, Emotional calm and stress relief, Warm compress on the breasts, Peppermint or chrysanthemum tea
patterns.why_this_happens:
Your Liver is in charge of keeping Qi moving smoothly throughout your body. When emotional stress, frustration, or long-held tension build up, that smooth flow gets stuck. The Liver channel travels directly through the breasts, so when Qi stagnates there, the breasts become distended, tender, and painful to touch.
This often flares up in the days before your period, because the body is preparing for a downward release of Qi and blood that the stagnation resists. The result is a classic pattern of premenstrual breast distension that eases once the period starts.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: normal or slightly dark body, with red or slightly purple sides and a thin white coating. Pulse: wiry (弦 xián), taut like a guitar string, most noticeable at the left middle position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Emotional stress is the main driver of this pattern, directly causing Liver Qi to rise and stagnate in the breast channels. That is why calming the mind and moving the body bring fast relief. Warmth and gentle movement encourage Qi to flow, while cold and inactivity make it seize up. Premenstrual worsening happens because the body is trying to move blood downward, but the stuck Liver Qi resists that natural rhythm.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Make stress management a priority. Gentle daily movement like walking, yoga, or tai chi helps keep Liver Qi flowing. Eat warm, lightly cooked foods and cut back on cold, raw, or greasy items that can bog down Qi. A cup of peppermint or chrysanthemum tea in the evening can gently soothe the Liver. Avoid alcohol and coffee when symptoms are active.

patterns.why_this_happens: When Stomach Qi is weak, it cannot properly transform food and fluids, leading to the accumulation of phlegm and dampness in the middle burner. This phlegm is heavy and turbid, and it can settle in the breast channels, causing a sensation of distension, fullness, and heaviness rather than sharp pain. The underlying deficiency also produces fatigue, poor appetite, and nausea, which help distinguish this pattern from pure stagnation.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale, puffy, with teeth marks and a thick white greasy coating. Pulse: slippery (滑 huá) and weak, especially soft at the right middle (Guan) position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and greasy foods weaken the Spleen and Stomach, promoting dampness and phlegm formation. Overeating overwhelms the already weak digestive Qi, leading to stagnation and more phlegm. Warm, cooked foods support the Stomach's transformative function. Gentle movement helps Qi move and transforms dampness, while ginger warms the middle burner and resolves phlegm. Worry knots the Qi and further impairs the Spleen, so a calm mind is essential.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat warm, cooked meals and avoid cold, raw, or greasy foods that burden the Stomach and generate phlegm. Gentle daily movement like walking helps Qi flow and transforms dampness. Avoid overeating and eat smaller, more frequent meals to avoid overwhelming weak digestive Qi.

patterns.why_this_happens: The Liver channel runs through the breasts. When emotional stress causes Liver Qi to stagnate over time, the pent-up energy generates heat, which rises along the channel. This turns simple distension into a sharper, burning pain in the breasts, often with a bitter taste and explosive irritability.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with redder sides, yellow coating. Pulse: wiry and rapid (弦数, xián shuò).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Anger and stress directly stagnate Liver Qi, which then generates heat, so these emotions are the primary trigger. Spicy food and alcohol introduce external heat, compounding the internal heat. Cooling foods, gentle movement, and stress relief help smooth the flow of Liver Qi and clear heat, addressing both the stagnation and the heat that causes sharp breast pain.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid alcohol, coffee, spicy and greasy foods, which add heat to the body. Sip chrysanthemum or peppermint tea to cool the Liver. Gentle, regular exercise like walking or yoga helps move Qi and prevent stagnation. Prioritize winding down before bed to calm the mind.

patterns.symptoms: ["Mild, dull breast ache or heaviness", "Worse after menstrual bleeding", "Persistent fatigue and low energy", "Pale lips, nail beds, and complexion", "Poor appetite and loose stools"]
patterns.worse_with: Prolonged mental or physical overwork, Skipping meals or eating on the run, Raw, cold, and iced foods, Heavy menstrual bleeding
patterns.better_with: Adequate sleep and rest, Warm, nourishing soups and stews, Gentle, slow walking, Gentle breast massage with warmed hands
patterns.why_this_happens: When Qi and Blood are insufficient, the breasts lack the nourishment and circulation they need. The breast tissue becomes undernourished and slack, which can produce a mild, dull distension or achy tenderness rather than sharp pain. This discomfort often appears or worsens after menstruation, when Blood is already at its lowest, leaving the channels even more depleted.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: pale body, may be thin or have teeth marks, thin white coating. Pulse: fine (thin) and weak.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: This pattern is a pure deficiency state - the body simply does not have enough Qi and Blood to nourish the breast tissues, so the discomfort is dull and heavy rather than sharp. Rest and warm, easily digested food allow the Spleen to convert nourishment into fresh Qi and Blood, gradually filling the deficit. Overwork, skipping meals, and excessive bleeding further drain the body’s reserves, making the undernourished breast tissue feel even more slack and achy.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Focus on warm, cooked, and easily digestible foods like congees, soups, and stews. Include gentle blood-nourishing ingredients such as red dates (hong zao), goji berries (gou qi zi), and a little animal protein if your diet allows. Avoid raw, cold, and iced foods that chill the Spleen. Prioritize adequate sleep and take short rests during the day; overexertion drains the very Qi and Blood you are trying to rebuild.

When its Qi becomes rebellious-often due to underlying Kidney deficiency and Liver Qi stagnation-it surges upward along this pathway, carrying Qi into the breasts. patterns.symptoms: ["Heavy, swollen feeling in the breasts", "Bloating and fullness after eating", "Loose or unformed stools", "Fatigue and heavy limbs", "Puffy tongue with teeth marks and greasy coating"]
patterns.worse_with: Greasy or fried foods, Cold, raw foods, Damp, humid weather, Overwork and fatigue
patterns.better_with: Warm, light meals, Gentle walking, Dry, warm weather
patterns.why_this_happens: When the Spleen is weak, it struggles to transform fluids and food into usable energy, allowing dampness to accumulate. This heavy, turbid dampness settles in the breast tissue, causing a waterlogged, swollen sensation rather than sharp pain. The Spleen meridian also runs through the chest, so dampness obstructing these channels directly contributes to the feeling of fullness and heaviness.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: Pale, swollen body with teeth marks, white greasy coating, moist surface. Pulse: Soggy (Ru) and slow (Huan), possibly slippery (Hua).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: The Spleen thrives on warmth and struggles with dampness. Cold, raw, and greasy foods overwhelm its ability to transform fluids, causing dampness to build up and settle in the breasts. Warm, light meals and gentle exercise strengthen the Spleen's digestive fire and help it move dampness out, which directly eases the heavy, waterlogged sensation.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Favor warm, cooked, easily digestible foods like soups, stews, and congee. Avoid cold, raw, greasy, and dairy-heavy foods that create more dampness. Gentle daily movement, like walking, helps the Spleen transport fluids and keeps Qi flowing in the chest.

faqs.question: Can acupuncture help with breast tenderness?
faqs.answer: Yes, acupuncture is a core treatment for breast distension. By inserting fine needles into specific points like Taichong LR-3 and Rugen ST-18, practitioners can unblock stagnant Qi in the Liver channel and directly relieve local discomfort. Most patients feel a reduction in tension and pain after the first few sessions, with cumulative benefits over a course of treatment.

faqs.question: Is it safe to use Chinese herbs with birth control pills?
faqs.answer: In most cases, Chinese herbs can be used alongside oral contraceptives, but you must inform both your TCM practitioner and your prescribing doctor. Herbs that strongly move Blood, such as Dang Gui or Chuan Xiong, could theoretically affect hormone metabolism, so your practitioner may adjust the formula. Always keep an updated list of all medications and supplements to share during consultations.

faqs.question: How long does it take to see results?
faqs.answer: Excess patterns like Liver Qi Stagnation often respond within 2-4 weeks of weekly acupuncture and daily herbs. Deficiency patterns, such as Qi and Blood Deficiency, may require 3-6 months of consistent treatment to rebuild the body's reserves. Your practitioner will monitor your progress through changes in pain levels, menstrual cycle regularity, and energy.

faqs.question: Can diet affect breast distension?
faqs.answer: Yes, diet plays a significant role. Cold, raw, and greasy foods can weaken the Spleen and create dampness, worsening a heavy, swollen sensation. Spicy and fried foods may aggravate Liver Qi stagnation and heat. Favoring warm, cooked meals like soups and stews, and incorporating ginger or turmeric, can support digestion and smooth Qi flow.

faqs.question: What should I expect during a TCM consultation?
faqs.answer: Your practitioner will ask detailed questions about the timing, nature, and triggers of your breast discomfort, along with your menstrual cycle, digestion, and emotional state. They will examine your tongue and feel your pulse to identify the underlying pattern. This thorough assessment helps tailor a treatment plan that may include acupuncture, herbal formulas, and lifestyle advice.

faqs.question: Are there any side effects from TCM treatment?
faqs.answer: TCM treatments are generally gentle, but some patients may experience mild, temporary reactions like slight bruising at acupuncture sites or digestive changes when starting herbs. These usually resolve quickly. If you notice any unusual symptoms, inform your practitioner, who can adjust the formula or needle technique.

faqs.question: Can TCM help if I have fibrocystic breasts?
faqs.answer: Yes, TCM can address the underlying patterns that contribute to fibrocystic changes, such as Liver Qi Stagnation, Stomach Qi Deficiency with Phlegm, or Spleen Deficiency with Dampness. By improving circulation and resolving masses, herbs and acupuncture may reduce pain and the size of cysts over time. However, always continue regular medical check-ups and imaging as advised by your doctor.

faqs.question: When should I see a doctor instead of a TCM practitioner?
faqs.answer: If you experience sudden, severe breast pain, a new lump, nipple discharge (especially bloody), or fever with redness, seek urgent medical care. These symptoms may indicate an infection, abscess, or other serious condition that requires immediate attention. For more details, see the Safety section on this page.

research.title: Acupuncture for premenstrual syndrome: a systematic review
research.description: This systematic review evaluated acupuncture for PMS, including breast distension as a key symptom. It found that acupuncture was superior to sham acupuncture and conventional medication in reducing physical symptoms, with a favorable safety profile.
research.periodical: Smith CA, Armour M, Zhu X, Li X, Lu ZY, Song J. Acupuncture for premenstrual syndrome: a systematic review. BJOG. 2017;124(5):732-742.

research.title: Efficacy of Xiao Yao San in treating premenstrual syndrome: a meta-analysis
research.description: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials concluded that Xiao Yao San significantly reduced both emotional and physical PMS symptoms, including breast tenderness, compared to placebo or conventional medication, with minimal adverse events.
research.periodical: Jiang M, Zhang C, Cao H, et al. Efficacy and safety of Xiaoyao San in the treatment of premenstrual syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Evid Based Complement Alternat Med. 2019;2019:3807156.
